summary:
The Falkland Islands are a British Overseas Territory with their own Legislative Assembly, which legislates locally; the United Kingdom is responsible for the territory's defence. The United Kingdom's Equality Act 2010 and Gender Recognition Act 2004 do not extend to the Islands, so legal protection and gender recognition depend on the territory's own ordinances.

Same-sex activity has been legal since 1989 and the age of consent has been equal since 2005.

Marriage and civil partnerships have been available since 29 April 2017. The Legislative Assembly passed the bill in March 2017 by 7 votes to 1, and the registrar general confirmed by reply in June 2017 that it is law. Civil partnerships are open to opposite-sex as well as same-sex couples, and a trans visitor whose relationship would be classed as same-sex under local birth-sex status can marry or register a civil partnership on the same terms. A public consultation ahead of the bill recorded 90% support for same-sex marriage and 94% for civil partnerships in a territory of roughly 3,000 residents.

Legal gender change has been possible since 2014 under the CPE Ordinance 2014. There is no self-identification route and no recognition of non-binary status. Holders of a UK Gender Recognition Certificate are recognised in their acquired gender under that ordinance.

The Constitution Order 2008, at Article 16, bans discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation. The provision covers sexual orientation only; no gender-identity ground is identified in it.

Two ordinances frame the criminal-justice treatment of bias. The Crimes Ordinance 2014 provides for hate-stirring on grounds of sexual orientation, and the CPE Ordinance 2014 makes sexual orientation an aggravating factor in sentencing. On the sources available, neither ground extends to gender identity.
tangentialFactors: The registrar general who confirmed the Falklands' marriage law also confirmed that same-sex marriage is not legal in South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands, a separate British Overseas Territory. A visitor moving between the two territories passes into a different legal regime on partner recognition.
localsOnly:
Stepchild and joint adoption have been available to same-sex couples since 2017.

A Prisons Ordinance was enacted in 2017.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not set out the requirements for legal gender change beyond the absence of self-identification and of non-binary recognition; the medical or evidentiary threshold is not described.

No gender-identity ground is identified in the Constitution Order 2008, the Crimes Ordinance 2014 or the CPE Ordinance 2014. Whether any other instrument covers gender identity is not sourced.

The content of the Prisons Ordinance 2017 is not detailed in the sources.

No data on trans-specific violence, hate-crime prosecutions or police practice in the territory appears in the sources.
